title: Introducing Agent Overwatch: Real-Time Supervision for Human and AI Agents
summary: Eyes on every conversation. Control at all times.
body_markdown:
‍


Contact centers are entering a new era of operations. AI agents are resolving customer requests, human agents are managing increasingly complex conversations, and both are working together to deliver better customer experiences.


‍


But the AI agents operating in today's contact centers aren't all built on the same platform. Enterprises are deploying AI agents from multiple providers, across different channels and business functions. At the same time, personal AI agents are emerging that can interact with businesses on customers' behalf.


As this model expands, an important question emerges: Who is watching these conversations as they happen?


‍


For decades, contact center supervisors have relied on live monitoring, agent escalations, and post-interaction quality assurance to manage their teams. These methods were designed for human-led operations, where supervisors could monitor a sample of calls, guide frontline teams, and review performance after the fact.


‍


Today, supervisors are responsible for a much broader operation. AI agents independently handle customer interactions, take actions across enterprise systems, and make decisions based on business policies. Meanwhile, human agents are managing sensitive situations, complex exceptions, and customers who need additional support.


‍


The challenge is that supervisors cannot be everywhere at once. And when AI agents operate across different vendors and platforms, maintaining consistent oversight becomes even more difficult.


‍


**Today, we're introducing Agent Overwatch, an AI-powered supervision capability from Observe.AI that gives contact center leaders real-time visibility and control across human agents, Observe.AI AI Agents, and third-party AI agents.**


‍


Agent Overwatch brings together live conversation monitoring, intelligent risk detection, automated supervisor alerts, and human intervention to help organizations identify situations requiring attention and respond while the customer is still engaged.


‍


## **The New Reality of Contact Center Supervision**


‍


Consider what happens during a typical day in a modern contact center.


‍


An AI voice agent built on a third-party platform is helping a customer update their account. The caller begins attempting to manipulate the AI into bypassing its instructions and revealing restricted information.


At the same time, a newly hired human agent is struggling with an unfamiliar customer request. The customer is becoming frustrated, and the agent is unsure which policy applies.


‍


Elsewhere, a VoiceAI agent repeatedly encounters a request it cannot successfully resolve and needs to escalate the interaction.


‍


And increasingly, a fourth scenario is becoming possible: a customer's personal AI assistant contacts a business on their behalf, communicating directly with an enterprise AI agent to complete a transaction. The two AI systems may interpret instructions differently, encounter conflicting information, or attempt an action requiring additional authorization.


‍


Each situation requires a different response. One may need immediate review for potential security or compliance risks. Another may benefit from a supervisor joining the conversation. The third may need to be transferred to a human agent who can resolve the issue.


‍


In a traditional contact center, these situations might only surface when an agent requests help, a customer complains, or a quality evaluation identifies the problem days later.


As AI takes on more responsibility, that model becomes increasingly difficult to sustain.


‍


Contact centers need the ability to understand what's happening across their operations, identify the interactions that warrant attention, and give supervisors the context and tools to act, regardless of which AI platform is involved.


‍


## **Meet Agent Overwatch: Live Intelligence With Human Control**


‍


Agent Overwatch extends Observe.AI's Agentic CX Platform with an active sup


ervision layer across human agents, Observe.AI VoiceAI and ChatAI, and supported third-party AI agents.


It connects four capabilities into a single operational workflow.


‍


### **Live Conversation Monitoring**


‍


Agent Overwatch analyzes active customer interactions against configurable operational, compliance, and risk criteria.


‍


For AI agents, whether built on Observe.AI or a supported third-party platform, this means monitoring conversations for unexpected behavior, failed resolution attempts, suspicious requests, and situations outside the AI's intended scope.


‍


For human agents, it means identifying conversations where an agent may be struggling, a customer needs additional attention, or a policy-sensitive interaction requires supervisor involvement.


‍


### **Intelligent Risk and Escalation Detection**


‍


Agent Overwatch evaluates conversation context alongside configured business rules to identify potential issues as they develop.


‍


These signals can include suspected AI jailbreak attempts, requests for unauthorized actions, repeated misunderstandings, missed compliance steps, or escalating customer frustration.


‍


Organizations can configure which situations require immediate attention, continued observation, or a standard escalation workflow.


‍


As enterprises deploy AI agents across multiple platforms, this provides a consistent approach to identifying risks and escalation needs across their contact center operations.


‍


### **Automated Supervisor Alerts**


‍


When a conversation meets defined escalation criteria, Agent Overwatch can trigger an alert to the appropriate supervisor.


‍


Through supported integrations with communication systems such as Slack or Microsoft Teams, supervisors can receive notifications that explain why an interaction was flagged and provide relevant conversation context.


‍


This helps supervisors focus on conversations where their involvement can make a meaningful difference, whether the interaction involves a human agent, an Observe.AI AI Agent, or a supported third-party AI agent.


‍


### **Live Supervisor Assist and Intervention**


‍


Identifying a problem is only useful if someone can act on it.


‍


Agent Overwatch gives supervisors access to conversation transcripts, relevant interaction history, and the reason for escalation so they can understand the situation without starting from scratch.


‍


Depending on the channel and contact center integration, supervisors can monitor an ongoing conversation, provide guidance, join a call, or initiate a human-assisted escalation.


‍


The objective is to make human judgment available at the moments when it is needed, regardless of which supported system is handling the conversation.


‍


## **One Approach to Supervising Human and AI Agents, Regardless of Vendor**


‍


The most important shift is how enterprises think about managing their workforce.


‍


‍


AI agents are becoming part of the contact center's operating model. They handle customer requests, follow defined workflows, access enterprise systems, and contribute directly to business outcomes.


‍


But these agents will not all come from one vendor.


‍


Organizations are increasingly managing AI agents across different platforms, each with its own instructions, analytics, safeguards, and escalation procedures. At the same time, human agents continue to manage complex customer interactions.


‍


Supervisors need consistent visibility into this entire environment.


‍


Human agents need coaching, guidance, and assistance when handling difficult conversations. AI agents need oversight that can identify unexpected behavior, recognize the limits of automation, and route sensitive situations to people.


‍


Agent Overwatch brings these needs together through a consistent approach to live monitoring and escalation across both Observe.AI and supported third-party AI agents.


‍


Supervisors can apply human judgment across different types of interactions while allowing successful conversations to continue without unnecessary intervention.


‍


And as personal AI agents begin interacting directly with enterprise AI systems, this approach becomes even more important. Businesses will need to monitor automated conversations where neither participant is necessarily human, while still maintaining appropriate authorization, compliance, and escalation controls.


‍


## **From Live Supervision to Continuous Improvement**


‍


Supervision is also an important source of operational intelligence.


‍


A flagged AI conversation may reveal a gap in business knowledge, an unsuccessful workflow, or a scenario that needs additional testing, regardless of which AI vendor handled the interaction.


‍


A supervisor intervention during a human-led call may highlight a coaching opportunity, an unclear policy, or an emerging customer issue.


‍


Within Observe.AI, these interactions can inform Quality Agents, Performance Agents, and Insights Agents, helping organizations evaluate outcomes, understand recurring problems, and improve performance over time.


‍


This connects what happens during a conversation to how the contact center improves after it ends.


‍


As enterprises expand AI automation across multiple platforms, they should be able to do so with confidence that supervisors remain informed and empowered to act.


‍


Agent Overwatch is an important step toward that operating model, providing real-time oversight across human agents, Observe.AI AI Agents, and supported third-party AI agents.


‍


**Eyes on every conversation. Control at all times.**
